items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 16, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: This was taken on a tour with Randy Weston, when Dizzy Gillespie was sick. We were in Europe at the time. This is Randy of course, this is Talib Kibwe, this is Stafford James and me

ctx.x: Oh yeah, as I was digging out, I don’t know I was going through looking for other things and I happened to find, I’ve got a whole archive in my house man, because I’m one of those people who saved everything. I’ve got newspaper clippings from Count Basie when I was with his band in the 50s in Europe. In fact I’ve got some pay receipts from Lionel Hampton from 1948, just because I kept all these things. Anyway, these are the members of Count Basie’s band. These are alumni. Because I think in this picture there’s…

band leader friend. This was taken on a tour with Randy Weston, when Dizzy Gillespie was sick. We were in Europe at the time. This is Randy of course, this is Talib Kibwe, this is Stafford James and me, and Eric Assasnte, that’s his name, Eric Ajie is the comic. Eric Assante. When Dizzy was sick we took this picture, we love you Dizzy, to send to him. Again, this is taken at the same party and the same people. I don’t know who this gentleman is at the top here. Do you recognize him?

items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: a lot of times he’ll perform with just himself, an alto player Talib Kibwe, and an African percussionist.

ctx.x: I want to ask you something. Now for some people that type of guidance is too loose. For other people that’s exactly what they want.

Well he knows what he’s got. He knows he couldn’t say that to anybody you know. So I feel like I am chosen by him and, to make matters better, he pays very well. If he can’t — he performs in all configurations, from solo to symphony. So sometimes, a lot of times he’ll perform with just himself, an alto player Talib Kibwe, and an African percussionist.

And he performs all over the world, Venezuela, and, but, if the budget can afford to pay me decently, then I’m added. I’m like the fifth member I think that’s added to the band. But if he can’t pay what he’d like to pay, he just won’t hire you. This is good. I like it. So I know whenever he calls it’s a well paying gig and no nonsense.
